content.text:
Assuming you mean `create-verification-skill` and `create-formal-verification-skill`: **one verifies observable app behavior; the other checks a specific invariant within an explicit scope.**

| | Practical verification | Formal verification |
|---|---|---|
| Main question | Can a user complete this journey, with the correct result and side effects? | Can this rule break under any input or sequence covered by the check? |
| Approach | Run the app and drive its UI, CLI, or API; capture evidence. | Use a model checker, code verifier, or proof tool suited to the property. |
| Reusable output | A project `verify` skill, launch/cleanup instructions, helpers, and feature map. | An area-named skill, reproducible checks, coverage record, and assumptions. |
| Limit | Selected journeys leave other cases unexplored. | A pass covers the stated model, bounds, and assumptions. |

Both must be exercised before delivery. The formal skill also requires showing that its check catches a deliberately broken version. See the [practical generator](/Users/jamie/.codex/plugins/cache/skillshare-pstack-fe9f343631f3cbe0/pstack/0.9.101/skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) and [formal generator](/Users/jamie/.codex/plugins/cache/skillshare-pstack-fe9f343631f3cbe0/pstack/0.9.101/skills/create-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md).

Exposed’s current [verify skill](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/.agents/skills/verify/SKILL.md) belongs to the practical side: it builds an isolated snapshot-backed app and compares selected public loader results with live production. Separate current-term checks test date inclusion rules, because matching production alone cannot establish those rules are correct.
